The new analyst should base each recommendation on a systematic, data‑driven scoring model that weights forward‑looking earnings revisions, sector‑relative price momentum, and macro risk flags, while ignoring isolated single‑company news spikes; they stay neutral whenever the composite score falls within a narrow band around zero.

The new analyst should weight quantitative sentiment scores (e.g., Twitter volume, news keyword frequency, and model‑derived polarity) over any single analyst’s intuition, ignore low‑volume or ambiguous headlines, and stay neutral unless the combined score exceeds a predefined confidence threshold (e.g., >70% bullish or bearish) before issuing a trade call.

The new tracker should weight order‑flow imbalances, execution‑size and price‑impact metrics while ignoring isolated large block trades, and only take a directional bet when the net imbalance exceeds a statistically‑significant threshold; otherwise it stays neutral.

The new analyst should base decisions on a systematic, data‑driven model that weights risk‑adjusted expected returns, macro‑fundamental indicators, and volume‑weighted price trends, while ignoring anecdotal news and gut feelings; they stay neutral (no position) whenever the model’s confidence score falls below a predefined threshold (e.g., 60% probability of positive Sharpe improvement).
